sources.title: Bounded CPU arithmetic and API variations

claims.statement: A two-dimensional matrix product applies row-by-column weighted sums, contracting the matching material axes; each store retains its own row and the output columns denote separate metrics. Models can use an affine layer to map numerical input features into numerical output features.
claims.scope: The presented 2D matrix and per-sample affine feature mapping; not a universal recipe for arbitrary tensor ranks or a claim about learned feature semantics.

evidence.supports: Two 2D tensors produce a matrix-matrix product; contracted matrix dimensions and retained external dimensions.
Input samples have in_features and output samples have out_features, using y=xA^T+b.
The concrete row/column sums and material interpretation.

claims.statement: For the stated recipes and cost/sweetness weights, the result is [[40,1],[80,6]], shape [2,2]. Each cost adds three material costs in cents; the hypothetical sweetness is 1 and 6. Shortening the right matrix to two rows is incompatible; changing one store does not mix the other store.
claims.scope: Exactly 2 stores/cups, 3 material terms and 2 indicators. Values are sums rather than averages or performance scores.

evidence.locator: arithmetic.md: four dot products; bounded_checks.py: integer products and changed_recipes
evidence.supports: Independent three-term sums, cost units and row independence.
Original first fence prints the stated values and shape.
Exact numeric agreement and necessary negative/row-change variations.

verification.observed: Exact expected values and shape; actual RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (2x3 and 2x2).
verification.details: Used independent Python integer three-term sums plus unmodified original torch fence and bounded CPU variations. No denominator: each output adds 3 products; cost unit cents, sweetness hypothetical.
verification.tolerance: Exact equality, tolerance 0; all numbers are small integers exactly representable as float32.

claims.statement: nn.Linear(3,2) uses y=xA^T+b by default, stores its weights as [out_features,in_features]=[2,3], stores a bias for each of its two outputs, and converts each three-feature sample to two outputs. For the 2D weights here, .T exchanges the rows and columns.
claims.scope: The default bias=True Linear(3,2) and this two-dimensional weight matrix. The section calls it a linear layer while correctly explaining the additive bias (affine computation).

evidence.supports: Affine formula, per-sample input/output dimensions, weight/bias shapes and forward implementation.
T reverses dimensions and therefore transposes the presented 2D matrix.

claims.statement: The second fence depends on the first, copies weights.T and [5,0] into the Linear parameters under no_grad, and outputs [[45,1],[85,6]] as a nested Python list. copy_ writes into the existing parameter; no_grad excludes these manual settings from reverse-mode recording, while the later forward can still record gradients. This is manual parameter setting, not learning.
claims.scope: Actual unmodified two-fence sequence and these ordinary API usages; no backward, optimizer or training occurs. no_grad is scoped to settings, not the later forward or forward-mode AD.

evidence.supports: Gradient recording is disabled inside the context and restored on exit; documented factory and forward-mode limitations.
copy_ copies source values into self and returns self; tolist returns nested Python lists.
Forward applies F.linear using the manually copied weights and bias.
Original second fence gives the exact expected nested list.

evidence.locator: bounded-stdout.json: original_linear, no_grad_restored, linear_forward_still_requires_grad, parameter_gradients_uncomputed; bounded_checks.py assertions
evidence.supports: Directly tested copy identity, shapes, context restoration, output list types and absence of computed parameter gradients.

verification.expected: [[45.0,1.0],[85.0,6.0]], weight shape [2,3], bias shape [2], copied identity same parameter; no_grad off in context/restored after; parameters still trainable with no computed grads.
verification.observed: All expected outputs and API assertions passed on CPU; forward requires_grad=True after leaving no_grad and parameter grads remain None.
verification.details: Ran both original fences in order, then independent short API checks. No backward, optimizer update, full training or download of data/models.

claims.statement: Changing only the cost bias from 5 to 8 changes the two outputs to [48,1] and [88,6], increasing each cost by 3 while leaving sweetness unchanged.
claims.scope: The same copied weight matrix, recipes and second sweetness bias of zero; only the first bias component changes.

evidence.supports: Bias is additive and per-output; other features and sample dimensions are retained.
Actual bias change yields exact predicted values and differences.

verification.details: Hand-derived independently and changed only the first bias component in the bounded CPU check.

factual_accuracy.details: All five substantive concept/API/arithmetic groups checked personally against original source and actual executions. Matrix operation and Linear default affine formula are consistent.

numeric_verification.details: Independent 3-material sums, axes, unit cents and hypothetical sweetness, result shape and bias exercise verified with exact equality. No empirical model scores or fractions.

figure_consistency.details: W.5 has no Markdown or HTML figures, SVG references or figure-dependent spatial claims. The tiny two-dimensional matrices are specified in the text/code; no render or view was needed or claimed.

source_verification.details: Personally fetched and read official PyTorch original files at installed immutable revision; all four snapshot SHA-256 values match installed source bytes. Exact ranges and HTTPS receipts retained. Candidate cache used only to locate; no prior verdicts read.

limitations.details: The recipe is an arithmetic illustration, not learned capability. Shapes apply to these 2D tensors; .T is used only on 2D weights. no_grad scopes manual reverse-mode settings and does not permanently disable later forward recording. No original paper, empirical result JSON, figure, training or model/data download is required.
